correctness.rationale: The cited unique oriented weak-order decomposition applies to exactly the associative quasitrivial operations in the claim. For related elements on distinct levels, choose the side of multiplication according to the projection orientation at each endpoint to force the whole endpoint level; multiplying by an intermediate element forces that element too. Thus a class meeting multiple levels is a union of whole consecutive levels. Conversely, a product across runs chooses the higher operand, a product within a collapsed run stays in that run, and a projection within an isolated level respects every partition. This gives unique labeled components: Bell partitions with the singleton orientation correction, and full collapses of sequences of at least two levels. The labeled sequence formula yields the bivariate EGF. B and J have positive coefficients at degrees one and two, forcing a strict modulus bound at every point of their respective first-root circles except the positive root; monotonicity and nonzero derivatives give the claimed simple-pole constants and their ratio. Independent coefficient arithmetic reproduced all nine totals, and decimal bisection reproduced the four displayed constants. value.rationale: Congruence size is a natural quotient invariant of a standard family of semigroups. The bivariate census captures every quotient class size count, not only the first few examples or the total number of operations. The mean asymptotic quantifies the contribution of the compatible congruences in a uniform labeled sample; it does not claim concentration or a typical-operation growth rate.
